instructions.name: admin_set_trading_fee_tiers
docs: Replaces the tiered trading fee: marginal bands (the last one open-ended),
a per-trade minimum and cap in micro-USD. An empty list turns it off.
The trade signer pays it in SOL, on top of the flat `trading_fee`.

instructions.name: admin_update_price_discontinued_after
docs: Seconds after which a withdrawal values an unrefreshed asset at $0
instead of reverting with PriceNeedsRefresh. Must exceed oracle_max_age.

instructions.name: admin_update_risk_settings
docs: Sets the audit-release risk settings: the daily swap loss limit (H-01),
the holding period after a deposit (M-08), the oldest price a deposit
and a swap accept (M-08, M-04), the widest price confidence (M-04), and
the smallest swap that counts as activity (L-10). Each has a fixed range.

instructions.name: create_admin_pool
docs: Creates an admin pool with specified fees and parameters.
This function initializes an admin pool, setting various fees and limits
that will apply to vaults created by this admin.
# Arguments
* `ctx` - The context for the admin pool creation
* `creation_fee` - Fee for creating a new vault
* `protocol_fee` - Fee for using the protocol
* `trading_fee` - Fee for trading activities
* `money_management_fee_max` - Maximum fee for managing money in vaults
* `performance_fee_max` - Maximum performance-based fee
* `withdraw_cooldown_max` - Maximum cooldown period for withdrawals
# Returns
Returns a `Result<()>` indicating success or failure of the admin pool creation

instructions.name: create_vault
docs: Creates a new vault with specified parameters
This function initializes a new vault with the given configuration parameters.
It sets up the vault's minimum contribution, raise period, minimum raise,
manager fee-withdrawal period, withdrawal cooldown and fees.
# Arguments
* `ctx` - The context for the vault creation
* `min_contribute_amount` - Minimum contribution, in base-token units; stored as USD and checked against the admin pool's `contribution_amount_min_usd`
* `raise_period` - Raise period in seconds; at most the admin pool's `fundrising_period_max`
* `min_raise_amount` - Minimum raise, in base-token units; stored as USD and checked against the admin pool's `raise_amount_min_usd`
* `mm_withdraw_period` - Manager fee-withdrawal period: one week, month, quarter or year, in seconds
* `withdraw_cooldown` - Seconds after the raise ends during which investors cannot withdraw; at most the admin pool's `withdraw_cooldown_max`
* `money_management_fee` - Yearly management fee; at most the admin pool's `money_management_yearly_fee_max`
* `performance_fee` - Performance fee; at most the admin pool's `performance_fee_max`
* `is_open_ended` - Whether the vault accepts deposits after the raise
# Returns
Returns a `Result<()>` indicating success or failure of the vault creation

with zero shares once its registry token accounts are closed; rent to
the money manager. Remaining accounts: [ata, mint] pairs, the vault's own token mint
first, then one per other registry mint.

version whose `VaultPool` struct uses the extension.

instructions.name: swap
docs: Executes a swap through Jupiter aggregator
# Arguments
* `ctx` - The context for the swap operation
* `data` - Serialized swap instruction data
* `amount_in` - The most the route may spend from the input account; the
vault grants the swap authority an allowance of exactly this amount
# Errors
Returns error if the swap operation fails
# Returns
* `Result<()>` - Success or error result

delegate when one is set. Authorization is asserted in the handler via
`VaultPool::can_trade` — it cannot be a `has_one` because either of two

This account also **pays** the SOL trading fee and any asset-registry
realloc rent. That is deliberate: if the delegate signed but the manager
paid, unattended bot trades would drain the manager's personal wallet and

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump to identify PDA

fields.name: price_discontinued_after
docs: Seconds after which a withdrawal treats a Pyth price as discontinued
and values the asset at $0 (paid in kind). Between `oracle_max_age` and
this age the withdrawal reverts with `PriceNeedsRefresh`, so a caller
who skips the refresh cannot choose the $0 valuation. Always greater
than `oracle_max_age` once set.
Carved from `padding`, so live admin pools read 0 until the admin sets
it (a deploy step). While it is 0 every stale price reverts: no price is
ever treated as discontinued.

fields.name: trading_fee_tier_count
docs: Tiered trading fee, paid by the trade signer in SOL on top of the flat
`trading_fee`. 0 = off. Carved from `padding`, so live admin pools read 0
until the admin sets the tiers (a deploy step).

fields.name: daily_loss_limit_bps
docs: H-01: most value, in bps of the vault's value, its swaps may lose in a
24-hour window.

fields.name: holding_period
docs: M-08: seconds after a deposit before that investor pool may withdraw.

fields.name: deposit_price_max_age
docs: M-08: oldest price, in seconds, a deposit accepts (and `oracle_max_age`).

fields.name: swap_price_max_age
docs: M-04: oldest price, in seconds, a swap accepts (and `oracle_max_age`).

fields.name: max_price_conf_bps
docs: M-04 / M-08: a deposit or swap price whose confidence is wider than
this, in bps of the price, is refused.

fields.name: activity_min_bps
docs: L-10: smallest swap input, in bps of the vault's value, that restarts
the idle period.

fields.name: oracle_config_version
docs: Goes up (wrapping) on every admin oracle change: approve, feed update,
close. A `PriceSnapshot` written under another value is refused, so an
admin oracle action takes effect at once for every vault. Was the last
spare byte (`padding`), so live admin pools read 0.

types.name: Claim
docs: Tokens a withdrawal owed to `recipient` but could not transfer, because the
issuer froze an account or paused the mint. The tokens stay in the vault
ATA and are counted in `VaultPool::reserved`, so no later pro-rata spends
them. `claim_withheld` pays `amount` once the transfer works again and closes
the account, returning the rent to `rent_payer`.
One account per `(vault_pool, mint, recipient, kind)`: later withdrawals add
to it. PDA `["Claim", vault_pool, mint, recipient, [kind]]`.

fields.name: kind
docs: `CLAIM_KIND_*`; also a seed of the address.

docs: `reassign_claim` moved a whole claim from `from` to `to` (same kind). The
tokens stay reserved in the vault; the `WithheldRecordedEvent` for `to` is
emitted just before this one.

docs: Emitted when an InvestorPool account is closed and its rent returned to
the investor: by `withdraw_token_fund` when the withdrawal takes the
investor's shares to zero, or by `close_investor_pool` for a pool that
already holds none. The address is a PDA, so a later deposit into the same
vault recreates the account at the same address.

fields.name: lamports
docs: Rent returned to the investor.

types.name: InvestorPoolCreatedEvent
docs: Emitted when a pool is created and initialized with a starting price

types.name: KaminoCollateral
docs: Marks a mint as the cToken of an approved Kamino reserve; PDA
`["KaminoCollateral", collateral_mint]`, created at the first approval.
Every pricing path checks this PDA for each registry mint, so a cToken is
always valued through its position and the reserve (never as a plain
token), and `approve_oracle_pool` refuses a cToken mint (so a cToken can
never be swapped or deposited).

fields.name: oracle_pool
docs: `OraclePool` of the underlying (prices the cToken)

types.name: KaminoPosition
docs: A vault's cTokens of one Kamino reserve, and the underlying it put in.
PDA `["KaminoPosition", vault_pool, reserve]`. The reserve binding is
copied from the approved `KaminoReserve` at the first supply, so valuation
and withdrawal never need the allowlist: a reserve disabled later never
locks investors in.
Invariant: `ctokens` = the vault's cToken balance minus the ledger amounts
of the cToken mint.

fields.name: ctokens
docs: cTokens held for the shareholders

fields.name: principal
docs: underlying (raw units) still invested through these cTokens

fields.name: rent_payer
docs: paid the account's rent at the first supply; receives it at reclaim

fields.name: fee_bps
docs: The platform's lending fee rate for the interest not yet charged: the
`LendingConfig` rate when the position opened or was last charged. A
fee change never applies to interest earned before it (Rado,
2026-11-07): the interest is charged at the lower of this rate and
the current one, and the position takes the current rate when it is
charged (design doc §5.3).

fields.name: fee_epoch
docs: `LendingConfig.fee_epoch` when it took `fee_bps`

types.name: KaminoPositionUpdatedEvent
docs: A withdrawal or a fee charge moved cTokens out of a position: the
platform's lending fee taken in cTokens first (owed to the admin), then the
position as it stays.

fields.name: liquidity_received
docs: underlying klend paid

fields.name: lending_fee
docs: platform lending fee recorded as owed to the admin, in the underlying

fields.name: ctokens
docs: position after the redeem

types.name: KaminoReserve
docs: An approved Kamino reserve; PDA `["KaminoReserve", reserve]`, written by the
admin. The binding is checked at every approval and copied into each
`KaminoPosition` at its first supply. `approved = false` stops new supply
into the reserve; redeems and withdrawals of existing positions continue.
`kamino_supply` (C-07) must also check that `oracle_pool` is still
approved: the admin may disable the underlying's oracle pool later.

fields.name: scope_prices
docs: the Scope account at approval, for information only: clients build
`refresh_reserve` from the live reserve (`klend::refresh_reserve_ix`)

fields.name: oracle_pool
docs: `OraclePool` of the underlying (prices the position)

fields.name: created
docs: true for the first approval of this reserve

fields.name: amount
docs: requested amount and liquid reserve (`keep`)

fields.name: liquidity_taken
docs: underlying klend took

fields.name: ctokens
docs: position after the supply

types.name: LedgerEntry
docs: What a vault owes per mint, apart from its shareholders:
- `claims_reserved`: tokens held for open investor `Claim` accounts
(a blocked investor leg of a withdrawal);
- `manager_owed`, `admin_owed`: fees charged but not paid yet, paid by
`claim_vault_fees`.

types.name: LendingConfig
docs: Protocol settings for Kamino lending; one account, written by the admin.
PDA `["LendingConfig"]`.
- `lending_fee_bps`: the platform's share of the interest a vault earns on
Kamino, settled when cTokens leave a position (design doc §5.4).
- `market`: the one Kamino lending market whose reserves can be approved.
Set once at init: a second market would break the withdrawal account
budget (design doc §5.6).
- `paused`: no new supply while set; redeems and withdrawals still work, so
a pause never locks funds in Kamino. Starts unpaused, fee 0.

fields.name: fee_epoch
docs: +1 at every fee change. A position records the epoch of its rate.

fields.name: fee_history
docs: The last `FEE_HISTORY` fee changes, oldest first (`fee_history_len` used).

fields.name: lowest_dropped_bps
docs: The lowest rate that left the history (`NO_RATE`: none yet).

fields.name: created
docs: true for the first write (`init_lending_config`; previous values 0, false)

types.name: ManagementFeeAccruedEvent
docs: Emitted when management fee is added to `pending_mm_fee_shares`: one slice
of time, `from` to `to`, charged to the investors holding shares in it.

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump to identify PDA

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump to identify PDA

fields.name: admin_pool
docs: The block timestamp of the observation

fields.name: max_slippage_bps
docs: This token's swap slippage limit in bps, taken from the padding (the
account keeps its size and layout). 0, the value of every pool created
before it existed, means the admin pool's `max_slippage_bps`. A swap
uses the higher limit of its two tokens (`swap_max_slippage_bps`).

fields.name: feed_id
docs: `FeedId` but avoid the type alias because of compatibility issues with Anchor's `idl-build` feature.

fields.name: publish_time
docs: The timestamp of this price update in seconds

fields.name: prev_publish_time
docs: The timestamp of the previous price update. This field is intended to allow users to
identify the single unique price update for any moment in time:
for any time t, the unique update is the one such that prev_publish_time < t <= publish_time.
Note that there may not be such an update while we are migrating to the new message-sending logic,
as some price updates on pythnet may not be sent to other chains (because the message-sending
logic may not have triggered). We can solve this problem by making the message-sending mandatory
(which we can do once publishers have migrated over).
Additionally, this field may be equal to publish_time if the message is sent on a slot where
where the aggregation was unsuccesful. This problem will go away once all publishers have
migrated over to a recent version of pyth-agent.

types.name: PriceSnapshot
docs: Prices of every registry mint, in registry order; one per vault, PDA
`["PriceSnapshot", vault_pool]`. Written by anyone from the pinned
accounts only, so no caller chooses a price. Zero-copy (`AccountLoader`):
a Borsh copy of this account overflows the 4 KB BPF stack.

fields.name: written_at
docs: clock time of the last write

fields.name: rent_payer
docs: receives the rent when the vault is reclaimed

fields.name: oracle_config_version
docs: `AdminPool.oracle_config_version` at the last write

types.name: PriceUpdateV2
docs: A price update account. This account is used by the Pyth Receiver program to store a verified price update from a Pyth price feed.
It contains:
- `write_authority`: The write authority for this account. This authority can close this account to reclaim rent or update the account to contain a different price update.
- `verification_level`: The [`VerificationLevel`] of this price update. This represents how many Wormhole guardian signatures have been verified for this price update.
- `price_message`: The actual price update.
- `posted_slot`: The slot at which this price update was posted.

types.name: SnapshotEntry
docs: One registry mint's Pyth price as written by `refresh_price_snapshot`. The
write decides nothing about age: every read applies today's rules with the
clock at read time (design doc §5.5a). Zero-copy layout, no implicit
padding (96 bytes).

fields.name: publish_time
docs: the Pyth publish time of the price (not the write time)

fields.name: approved
docs: `OraclePool.is_approved` at write time (0 / 1)

fields.name: is_ctoken
docs: 1: the mint is a Kamino cToken; the price is its underlying's, and
every reader values it through its position and reserve

fields.name: price_account
docs: the canonical Pyth account the price came from (identifies the feed)

types.name: TradingDelegateRevokedEvent
docs: Emitted when a money manager revokes their vault's trading delegate.

fields.name: previous_delegate
docs: The delegate that was just revoked.

types.name: TradingDelegateSetEvent
docs: Emitted when a money manager authorizes a trading delegate for their vault.

fields.name: previous_delegate
docs: Previous delegate, or all-zeros when none was set. Lets the listener
mirror a re-point (delegate A -> delegate B) without re-reading chain.

fields.name: money_manager
docs: The vault's money manager, always read from `VaultPool` state rather
than from whoever signed. Points, PnL and fee attribution key off this,
so it stays the real manager even when a delegate executed the trade.

fields.name: trader
docs: Who actually signed this trade — the money manager, or the vault's
trading delegate. Appended last so existing field offsets are unchanged.
Without this, a delegate-signed trade and a manager-signed trade are
indistinguishable in our records: if a delegate key were compromised we
could not say which trades were the attacker's, and a manager disputing
a trade could neither be confirmed nor refuted.

types.name: TradingFeeChargedEvent
docs: The tiered trading fee one swap charged its signer. Separate from
`TradingEvent` so that event keeps its layout.

fields.name: trader
docs: Who paid: the signer (manager or trading delegate).

fields.name: fee_usd_micro
docs: The fee after the minimum and cap, before conversion to SOL.

fields.name: trade_usd_micro
docs: The trade's value: input spent × input price.

types.name: TradingFeeTier
docs: One band of the tiered trading fee. Bands are marginal: `bps` applies only to
the part of the trade between the previous band's bound and this one.
`upper_bound_usd` is in whole USD. The last active band has no upper bound
and stores 0.

fields.name: migrated_mints
docs: the `VaultPool.reserved` slots moved into `claims_reserved`

types.name: VaultCreatedEvent
docs: Emitted when a pool is created and initialized with a starting price

fields.name: min_contribute_amount_usd
docs: Minimum contribution amount

types.name: VaultFeesClaimedEvent
docs: Owed fees paid by `claim_vault_fees`, per mint.

fields.name: manager_owed
docs: still owed after this call (a blocked transfer stays owed)

types.name: VaultFeesOwedEvent
docs: Fees recorded as owed (a withdrawal or a periodic charge), per mint.

fields.name: manager_owed
docs: totals owed after this event

types.name: VaultLedger
docs: One per vault, PDA `["VaultLedger", vault_pool]`. Replaces the two
`VaultPool.reserved` slots (which stay in the layout, zeroed). Zero-copy
(`AccountLoader`), like `PriceSnapshot`: no Borsh copy on the stack.

fields.name: in_use
docs: Bit i (little-endian u16): entry i's mint is the underlying of an open
Kamino position. Such a mint never leaves the registry, so taking part
of a position back never needs a free registry slot. Was 2 spare bytes
(zero on every ledger: nothing marked).

fields.name: rent_payer
docs: receives the rent when the vault is reclaimed (the manager at
`create_vault`, the operator at `init_vault_accounts`)

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump to identify PDA

fields.name: asset_registry
docs: Reference to the asset registry for this vault

fields.name: min_contribute_amount_usd
docs: Minimum contribution amount

fields.name: trading_delegate
docs: Optional second key allowed to trade this vault — and only trade.
Carved out of the head of `padding`, so the account's total size is
unchanged and **existing vaults need no realloc or migration**. Every
live account already holds zeroes here (verified against all 178 on-chain
`VaultPool`s), so they decode as "no delegate" the moment this ships.
All-zeros is the disabled sentinel rather than `Option<Pubkey>`: an
`Option` prefixes a discriminant byte and shifts every following field,
which would force exactly the migration this layout avoids.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Token amounts the vault holds but owes to someone: the legs of a
withdrawal (investor, manager, admin) that could not be transferred
because the issuer froze an account or paused the mint. Each is a
`Claim` account; the amount stays in the vault ATA until
`claim_withheld` pays it. Every pro-rata reads `available`, which
excludes it, so later withdrawals and fees never spend it twice.
Carved out of `padding` the same way as `trading_delegate`: the size is
unchanged and every live vault holds zeroes here, which decode as two
empty slots. A zero mint is an empty slot. Two slots bound the number of
different blocked mints per vault; a third reverts the withdrawal
(L-05, accepted by Rado 2026-10-10).

fields.name: closed_at
docs: When `close_vault` ran; the management fee accrues only up to it.
Carved out of the last `padding` word (zero on every live vault), so
the size is unchanged. Zero while open, and on a vault closed before
this field existed.

fields.name: pending_mm_fee_shares
docs: Management fee earned by the manager and the admin and not paid yet, in
shares (the units of `total_shares`). Every share price divides by
`total_shares + pending_mm_fee_shares`, so nobody buys into, or leaves
with, fee already earned. A deposit adds the fee for the time since the
last accrual and moves no fee tokens; the periodic charge pays all of it,
and a withdrawal pays the part that leaves with its shares, in the legs
it already pays. The first field of the 64-byte extension: zero on a
resized vault, which is "nothing owed".

fields.name: last_mm_fee_charge_at
docs: When the periodic charge last ran: the anchor of its once-per-period
schedule. Separate from `last_mm_fee_withdraw_at`, which every deposit
and withdrawal now moves when it notes the fee: anchored there, a
deposit just after a period boundary would push the next charge a whole
period away while the owed fee only grows. Zero on a resized vault until
its first accrual copies the timer it had (see `accrue_mm_fee`).

fields.name: value_usd
docs: H-01 / L-10: the vault's value in micro-USD when it was last priced —
by a deposit, a withdrawal or `refresh_vault_value` — excluding tokens
reserved for claims. The swap's daily loss limit and its activity size
are shares of it. Zero on a vault until its first pricing.

fields.name: value_at
docs: When `value_usd` was set.

fields.name: loss_window_start
docs: H-01: start of the current 24-hour loss window.

fields.name: loss_window_usd
docs: H-01: value, in micro-USD, the vault's swaps lost in the current window,
measured with the oracle prices. Gains do not offset it.

fields.name: kamino_positions
docs: Open Kamino positions (cTokens held for the shareholders), at most
`MAX_KAMINO_POSITIONS`. Was the first spare extension byte (live vaults
read 0).

fields.name: kamino_position_accounts
docs: `KaminoPosition` accounts that exist (open or empty); reclaim needs 0.
Was the second spare extension byte.

fields.name: mm_fee_carry
docs: Audit finding 9: the fraction of a management-fee share that the last
accrual rounded down, in units of 10^-9 share (always below 10^9). The
next accrual adds it back, so splitting the time into many accruals
charges the same as one. Was 4 spare extension bytes (live vaults read 0).

fields.name: activity_volume_usd
docs: Audit finding 7: micro-USD the vault's swaps sold since the last swap
that restarted the idle period. A swap restarts it when this sum reaches
`activity_min_bps` of `value_usd`, so five small trades count as one
large one. Was 8 spare extension bytes (live vaults read 0).

fields.name: extension_reserved
docs: Zero. The rest of the extension, for later fields.

types.name: VaultPoolResizedEvent
docs: Emitted when `resize_vault_pool` grows an account to `VAULT_POOL_ALLOC_LEN`.

types.name: VaultRentReclaimedEvent
docs: Emitted by `reclaim_vault_state` when the VaultPool and AssetRegistry are
closed. `lamports` is the rent of both, returned to the money manager. The
vault's address is never reused: `vaults_amount` on the manager pool only
grows.

types.name: VaultTokenAccountReclaimedEvent
docs: Emitted by `reclaim_vault_token_accounts` for every vault token account it
closed. `burned` is the dust destroyed before the close: with zero shares
outstanding it belonged to nobody. The rent went to the money manager.

types.name: VaultValueRefreshedEvent
docs: Emitted by `refresh_vault_value`: the vault's value, in micro-USD, that
the swap's daily loss limit and activity size are measured against.

types.name: VerificationLevel
docs: Pyth price updates are bridged to all blockchains via Wormhole.
Using the price updates on another chain requires verifying the signatures of the Wormhole guardians.
The usual process is to check the signatures for two thirds of the total number of guardians, but this can be cumbersome on Solana because of the transaction size limits,
so we also allow for partial verification.
This enum represents how much a price update has been verified:
- If `Full`, we have verified the signatures for two thirds of the current guardians.
- If `Partial`, only `num_signatures` guardian signatures have been checked.
# Warning
Using partially verified price updates is dangerous, as it lowers the threshold of guardians that need to collude to produce a malicious price update.

types.name: WithdrawFeeSplitEvent
docs: Emitted by `withdraw_token_fund` for every asset, next to
`WithdrawTokenFundEvent`, whose `admin_fee` combines the protocol's
management and performance shares. Amounts in token base units.

fields.name: claimed_amount
docs: Part of `fee_amount + admin_fee` not transferred because the token is
frozen or paused; it stays in the vault ATA, reserved for `Claim`s.

fields.name: amount
docs: Paid to the investor (after the performance fee).

fields.name: money_manager_fee
docs: Management fee paid to the manager on top of `amount`: their part of
the owed fee leaving with the shares. Not taken from the investor's part
since the deferred fee (2026-10); the performance fee still is.

fields.name: price_available
docs: False when the asset had no fresh price: it was paid in kind and
counted as $0 for the performance fee. `token_price` is 0 then.

fields.name: claimed_amount
docs: Part of `amount + money_manager_fee + performance_fee + admin_fee` that
was not transferred because the token is frozen or paused. It stays in
the vault ATA, reserved for the recipients' `Claim` accounts.

types.name: WithheldClaimedEvent
docs: `claim_withheld` paid the whole claim to `recipient` and closed it.

fields.name: kind
docs: `CLAIM_KIND_*` of the paid claim.

types.name: WithheldRecordedEvent
docs: A withdrawal (or manager fee withdrawal) left `amount` of `mint` owed to
`recipient`. `total_amount` is the claim's balance after this addition.

fields.name: kind
docs: `CLAIM_KIND_*` stored on the claim.
